correctness.rationale: Exact outcome enumeration establishes E L=a+dt, E U=1-b+dt, E L^2=a+dt^2, E U^2=1-b+dt^2, E(LU)=a(1+t^2)+t(b-2a), hence Cov=ab+(d^2-a)t(1-t). Reflection symmetry gives the exact quadratic product of the two variances in z=t(1-t), so the derivative sign of the squared correlation is the affine H(z). At zero H=2ab(1-b)(h+ab)>0. At z=1/4 H=r x^5 B, with x=d=(2^n-1)/3^n<1/3, r=3^n/(2^n-1)^2<3/5. The explicit B lower estimate B>=1/10+(33/100)x>0 holds uniformly for every integer n>=4. Thus the correlation is strictly increasing in z and maximized only at t=1/2. Exact substitution produces R_n, and a/b^2=(3/4)^n tends to zero, yielding asymptotic R_n~(2/3)^n. SymPy reconstructed seven polynomial identities from the actual verify.py; 272 exact checks corroborate finite cases but are not the proof of all n.

originality.rationale: The complete 2022 Papadatos article treats sample size two, while its concluding discussion formulates the later-sample-size monotone lattice question. The sharp bound proved here holds for every n>=4 on exactly three equally weighted atoms. General order-statistic correlation bounds give 1/n, which does not imply the sharp exponentially smaller coefficient. The inspected 2026 published note proves a different two-draw probability-vector optimization. The 2021 discrete-parent automatic-differentiation article is a credible nearby source, but its complete text was unavailable; the accessible first-page preview and abstract do not settle this sharp all-n support-geometry statement. Residual priority risk persists, as recorded, but no inspected logically covering theorem was found.
residual_risks: The complete 2021 López-Blázquez--Salamanca-Miño paper was unavailable for substantive full-text comparison; it may contain further examples, calculations, or a hidden equivalent statement.
Earlier studies of three-state order-statistic dependence might use unindexed language or separate mathematical transformations and independently imply the result.
Published-database search and own-ledger deduplication do not establish publication priority or independence from other unpublished work.

value.rationale: Papadatos 2022 formulates a natural lattice-optimality problem for correlations of order statistics from finite uniform populations beyond sample size two. The result rigorously resolves its entire three-support-point extreme-rank slice for every integer sample size n>=4, determines the unique extremizing support geometry and sharp constant, and proves exponential improvement over the universal 1/n bound. Covering an unbounded family, rather than incrementing a known n=3 instance to a single n, provides substantive structural value without claiming extension to arbitrary supports or weights.
